title: LayerNorm scale-shift canary degradation writeup
content:
Summary:

During a canary rollout of model v3.4.1 (quantized, fused-kernel build) we observed a reproducible degradation in generation quality that correlated with a downstream drop in token-level likelihoods and an increase in repetitive tokens for a subset of prompts. The issue surfaced only in the canary cohort (2% traffic) and did not initially trigger latency or error SLO breaches.

High-level impact:
- Affected 2% of traffic routed to canary pool between ~04:12–06:40 UTC on 2024-10-21.
- Quality regressions (user-visible hallucinations and repetition) for ~18% of sampled prompt set used by eval harness.
- No system-level errors, no OOMs, p95 latency unchanged — visible only via quality telemetry and human smoke tests.

Detection:
- Automated eval job (nightly canary-quality-check) flagged a drop in BLEU-like score and an increase in repetition metric at 04:25 UTC.
- On-call SRE (Ravi) received a Delta alert from the quality pipeline and escalated to eng-sre + applied-ml.
- Quick manual inspection of streaming samples showed odd token probability distributions: a chunk of outputs had near-uniform low-confidence logits followed by repeated eos-like tokens.

Initial hypothesis and triage steps:
- Suspected tokenization mismatch or broken tokenizer-to-model mapping (common cause for sudden discrete distribution changes).
- Also considered weight corruption during manifest staging or quantization metadata mismatch (scale offsets).
- Hypothesis prioritized: LayerNorm scale parameter shifted during a weight transform step (quantization/runtime fusion) causing activations to fall into a regime where softmax becomes flat for some heads.

Timeline (key events):
- 03:50 UTC: v3.4.1 scheduled rollout to canary pool (2%).
- 04:12 UTC: Canary traffic starts; first automated eval run completes showing 12% quality drop vs baseline.
- 04:25 UTC: Alert triggered and paging to on-call.
- 04:30–05:15 UTC: Rapid triage: collected model artifact checksums, manifest, and metadata for the canary pool.
- 05:20 UTC: Replayed request trace on a local dev box using the canary artifact — reproduced lower token likelihoods and repetition.
- 05:45 UTC: Dumped weight shards and compared layernorm gamma/beta tensors to baseline model v3.4.0. Observed systematic scale factor differences in several LayerNorm gamma tensors in the final transformer blocks.
- 06:10 UTC: Rolled back canary to v3.4.0. Quality metrics returned to baseline in subsequent eval run at 06:38 UTC.
- 06:40 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; postmortem drafting started.

Investigation details and evidence:
- Artifact verification:
  - Manifest checksum matched across storage nodes but the transformation pipeline that creates the fused/quantized artifact had a non-idempotent scaling step introduced in PR #789 (runtime repo). The PR modified the post-quantization rescaling pass to normalize by an L2-derived factor; this was intended to reduce outliers but did not account for per-channel LayerNorm parameters.

- Weight diffing:
  - Compared text-format dumps of LayerNorm gamma vectors between v3.4.0 and v3.4.1 canary artifact. Observed a repeating ~1.06x multiplicative shift in gamma values for the last 6 transformer blocks. Not present in original open-source checkpoint used as input to the transform.
  - Example excerpt (block 23 gamma first 8 dims):
    - baseline: [0.987, 1.003, 0.995, 1.000, 0.992, 1.010, 0.991, 1.004]
    - canary:   [1.046, 1.064, 1.053, 1.060, 1.051, 1.074, 1.053, 1.064]

- Reproduction locally:
  - Loaded the canary artifact into local runtime with identical kernel selection flags. Re-ran the failing prompt set. Output reproduced the flat/low-confidence logits and repetition.
  - Swapping only the LayerNorm gamma tensors in-memory with baseline tensors restored normal likelihood distributions and non-repetitive outputs.

Root cause (current understanding):
- A bug introduced in the post-quantization normalization code path (PR #789) applied a global L2 normalization to the entire weight blob which interacted badly with per-channel LayerNorm gamma semantics. The normalization was executed after per-shard packing and before manifest write, causing a deterministic multiplicative scale to be applied to a subset of tensors (those in certain shard offsets). The non-uniformity of shard sizes and alignment produced the observed pattern (only later blocks affected).

Contributing factors:
- Insufficient unit tests for post-quantization transforms that validate per-tensor statistical properties (mean/variance/gamma/beta ranges).
- Missing canary checks that diff layer-wise parameter distributions between source checkpoint and transformed artifact. Current artifact validation only checks global checksums and top-level shapes.
- New fused-kernel build path had limited coverage in dev-simulated smoke tests where only a handful of short prompts are used; the evaluation prompt set used in nightly canary is broader and caught the issue.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back canary to previous artifact (v3.4.0) at 06:10 UTC. Canary pool was drained and re-verified.
- Disabled the post-quantization L2 normalization step (hotfix in transform pipeline) and re-ran the artifact build in a staging environment; the rebuilt artifact matched baseline LayerNorm stats.
- Added temporary pre-release check in the artifact publisher to compare per-tensor norm ratios with a threshold and refuse publish if abnormal. This prevented the bad artifact from reaching other pools.

Longer-term remediation and action items (owners assigned):
1) Add per-tensor statistical validation to transform pipeline (owner: Sofia Chen, due: 2024-11-05). Tests should assert acceptable multiplicative drift per tensor and per-block.
2) Revert PR #789 and rework normalization algorithm to be per-channel aware (owner: runtime team / Marcus O'Neill, due: 2024-11-08).
3) Expand canary eval harness to include a targeted distribution-check test that computes layerwise gamma/beta drift and token-likelihood sanity checks (owner: applied-ml / Elena García, due: 2024-11-07).
4) Add a gating step in the release pipeline to perform a synthetic replay of 100 canonical prompts through the built artifact and compare token-probability histograms to baseline (owner: eng-sre, Ravi Patel, due: 2024-11-06).
5) Instrument runtime to emit a per-request lightweight checksum signature of key tensors used during inference (e.g., a small hash of the last-block LayerNorm gamma vector) so future canary telemetry can correlate tensor-level fingerprints to quality signals (owner: runtime infra team, due: 2024-12-01).
6) Run a full backfill of recent artifacts (last 6 months) to check for similar drift patterns and ensure no other releases accidentally applied the same transform (owner: release-eng, due: 2024-11-15).

Runbook updates (immediate):
- Add an entry under "Model Artifact Validation" with steps to dump and diff LayerNorm/gamma stats pre- and post-transform. Include example commands.
- Update canary quality alert runbook to include a quick per-tensor stat check (script path: infra/tools/artifact-diff.sh).

Commands and snippets used during triage (for reproducibility):
- Dump gamma: python -m runtime.tools.dump_tensor --artifact s3://artifacts/v3.4.1/canary --tensor transformer.block.23.layernorm.gamma > gamma_block23.txt
- Compute L2 ratio: python -m runtime.tools.tensor_stats --a gamma_block23.txt --b baseline_gamma_block23.txt --metric l2_ratio
- Local replay: python -m runtime.cmdline.run_local --artifact /tmp/v3.4.1-canary --prompts tests/canary_prompt_set.jsonl --seed 42 --kernel fused

Open questions (unresolved):
- Why did the normalization only affect a subset of shards? Hypothesis: non-uniform shard padding/alignment in packer logic. Need a deeper audit of packer offsets. (owner: platform-engineering)
- Were there any other small multiplicative drifts introduced in other tensors beneath detection threshold? We plan to run full-stat scans across all tensors in recent artifacts.

Lessons learned:
- Small multiplicative shifts in normalization parameters can produce outsized degradation in generation quality even when latency and basic numeric checks look normal.
- Quality evals are critical — infrastructure-only checks (shapes, checksums) are insufficient for transformed/quantized artifacts.
- Gating artifact publication on per-tensor validation buys a lot of confidence for canary deployments.

Post-incident communication plan:
- Send summary email to runtime, applied-ml, release-eng, and eng-sre mailing lists with links to this doc and linked artifacts (owner: Ava Martinez, by 2024-10-24).
- Present a 20-minute incident review in the weekly infra sync with runtime team to walk through the problematic transform and the corrected approach (owner: Marcus O'Neill, scheduled: 2024-10-30).

Appendix: quick diff output (truncated)
- block23.gamma.mean: baseline=~0.999, canary=~1.061
- block23.gamma.std: baseline=~0.028, canary=~0.030
- per-tensor l2_ratio across artifact: median=1.00, 95p=1.002, max=1.074 (only LayerNorm gammas in last 6 blocks above 1.04)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the manual dump scripts — they were invaluable for fast repro. Need to wrap them into CI.
- We were lucky the nightly quality job exists; otherwise this may have hit prod silently.

End of writeup.
